sources.title: Ma Yi Yi, Burmese Sources for the History of the Konbaung Period 1752 to 1885 (1965)
sources.note: Publisher extract read. Used only for Alaungpaya, Shwebo/Konbaung and dynastic foundation; its older account dates Ava’s capture differently from later scholarship, which is not adopted here.

sources.title: British Museum, Burma to Myanmar: 1,500 years of connection and isolation
sources.note: Original museum article read through indexed text. Sections Conquest and cultures and Colonial eclipse. Direct fetch was intermittent.

sources.title: National Army Museum, A timeline of Burma and the Army
sources.note: Direct institutional timeline read, especially 1826, 1852 to 53 and 1885 to 95. Do not adopt its precise annexation proclamation days; secondary institutional chronologies differ. The card uses the secure year 1886 for Upper Burma and 1852 to 53 for the second war.

sources.title: Frances O’Morchoe, Two Golden Commissions, British Library
sources.note: Direct article read. Paragraphs on overlapping Shan allegiances, 1882 commissions and resistance after Thibaw’s removal. Its compressed early-war dates are not used.

sources.title: Jacques P. Leider, King Alaungmintaya’s Golden Letter to King George II (1756), GWLB (2009)
sources.note: Original library-hosted PDF downloaded and read. Printed pp.74 to 76 translation, p.102 packaging, p.122 Burmese transcript and p.123 romanization. Transcript page visually inspected. Burmese ဆင်ဖြူ corresponds to chaṅ-phrū and “white elephants” in royal titulature.

sources.title: Myanmar Department of Archaeology, National Museum and Library, Kuthodaw Memory of the World nomination
sources.note: Original nomination indexed text read, section 3.2, printed p.2. Distinguishes completion in 1868 from the 1871 council; inscriptions are Pali in Burmese script.

sources.title: Royce Wiles, Chris Clark, Tamara Ditrich and Mark Allon, The Pāli Tipiṭaka Recension Carved on the Kuthodaw Pagoda
sources.note: Original research PDF indexed introduction read. Mindon reign 1853 to 1878, 1860 to 1868 carving, 729 marble stelae and new capital at Mandalay.

sources.title: Su Lin Lewis, Where Knowledge Thrives, British Council
sources.note: Historian’s institutional essay read. Only Histories of Education opening paragraphs used; no later chronology taken from this page. The exhibition booklet reproduces the same essay and is not counted as a separate source.

sources.title: San San May, Kammavaca: Burmese Buddhist ordination manuscripts, British Library
sources.note: Direct curator essay read. Opening two paragraphs, Add.15289 and Or.12010E captions; general ritual description bounded by explicitly dated eighteenth- and nineteenth-century examples.

sources.title: John Clarke, Highlights of the Lacquer Collection from Myanmar in the Victoria and Albert Museum (2017)
sources.note: Original collection study by V&A curator read directly. Illustrations 3, 4, 8 and associated text. Colonial horsehair technique and 1908 to 1911 bowl not projected backward.

sources.title: San San May, Traditional games in Burma, republished by Scroll (2018)
sources.note: Read the curator’s original essay in its acknowledged republication. Original BL 2018/07 URL now redirects; archive and new post URL fail. Court paintings discussed separately from the explicitly 1890s photograph. No unsupported exact manuscript year added.

sources.title: British Library, Mss MAN/BUR 617, Burmese medical manuscript (1878)
sources.note: Direct catalogue read. 255 folios, seven titles, Burmese language, 1878, palm leaf with nine lines per side, gilt edges and binding boards. No remedies or efficacy inferred.

sources.title: British Museum, illustrated parabaik, museum number 2011,3015.1
sources.note: Original indexed catalogue consulted. Direct fetch 403. Production-date and curator-comment fields verify about 1880, accession of Thibaw in 1878, minister U Shwe Maung, sumptuary privileges and promotion.

proposedOverrides.name: Burma (Konbaung kingdom)
proposedOverrides.summary: Konbaung Burma was a major mainland kingdom, with court workshops, monastic learning and far-reaching diplomacy. Its imported outline and dates obscure successive British conquests.

batchIdentityNotes.name: Konbaung-era Burma
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Konbaung dynasty 1752 to 1885; British annexation of remaining Upper Burma 1886.
batchIdentityNotes.geometryEvidence: Three decoded polygons: world-1783 (1783 to 1800), world-1800 (1800 to 1815), world-1815 (1815 to 1878). See identity.json for exact bounds. The last snapshot retains a coast down to about 10.12 N after 1826 and 1852 to 53 territorial losses.
batchIdentityNotes.publicCaveats: Overview and final historical section explicitly distinguish atlas coverage from dynasty, lost southern territories, and overlapping tributary influence. No modern nation or earlier Burmese dynasty association proposed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronologyCaveat: 1852 versus 1853 and 1885 versus 1886 are separated as war/conquest versus administrative annexation; exact proclamation days differ between institutional summaries and are omitted.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Golden Letter, original 1756 diplomatic document; Burmese phrase ဆင်ဖြူ / white elephants verified in transcript line 2 and Leider translation p.74. Pali manuscripts are explicitly labelled Pali in Burmese script.
batchIdentityNotes.collision: Initial index/runtime/staged check found exact burma uncovered; no aliases attached.
batchIdentityNotes.unfilledTopics: No verified domestic toilet or sanitation evidence added. No medical remedy reconstructed. Source leads with ambiguous dates and broad modern customs excluded.
